correctness.rationale: Read RESULT.md spectral proof. Iteration residual is -(I-eta A)^k b and solution multiplier eta sum_(j=0)^(k-1)(1-beta)^j b at eigenvalue beta=eta lambda in [0,alpha]. This sum is strictly positive for beta<2, preventing 0/0 even for inconsistent systems. The residual-to-normwise-solution ratio is a positive-weight maximum of the scalar g(beta). On [0,1] it decreases and is bounded by 1/(alpha k); for beta>1 the formula increases in u=beta-1, yielding the top-eigenvalue endpoint. Both endpoints are attained by explicit PSD examples. On alpha>1 the first branch decreases and second increases, giving one crossing root; log expansion gives asymptotic. k=2 scalar witness sets sharp all-k bound u<=1/sqrt(3), while all even/odd k satisfy (k+1)u^k<=1 and (k-1)u^k<=1 by elementary recurrence monotonicity. k=1 has no admitted minimizer. Independent scalar spectral tests for k=1..40 and six alpha values over 401-point grids corroborated endpoints; grid search is not the minimax proof.

value.rationale: Provides exact optimal constant stepsizes for a mathematically motivated universal backward-error metric, improves the unit-step all-k guarantee by a sharp 1+1/sqrt(3) relaxation and asymptotically halves the best horizon-k constant. Crucially, includes inconsistent singular systems which classical forward-error treatments omit.

final_claim: For real symmetric nonzero PSD A, nonzero b (including inconsistent equations), zero-start Richardson with eta=alpha/||A||_2 and 0<alpha<2 has exact universal matrix-only normwise backward error at horizon k>=1 equal to max(1/(alpha k), |1-alpha|^k/(1-(1-alpha)^k)), attained by singular 2x2 and scalar witnesses. For k>=2 the unique optimizing alpha=1+u_k solves u_k^k[k(1+u_k)+(-1)^k]=1 and approaches 2-log(2k)/k. A 1/k bound simultaneously at all horizons holds exactly for 1<=alpha<=1+1/sqrt(3).
